answers.answerContent: The farmer was suddenly coiled and wrapped around by a large python while searching for his lost cow on the mountain.
he chose not to kill the snake because he remembered the eight precepts he had undertaken that morning and decided to protect his morality even at the cost of his life
He escaped because the power of his strict morality protected him after he chose not to kill to keep his precepts.
If he had killed the snake, he would have broken his precepts and lost the spiritual protection of his virtue.
If we were in the farmer's place, we would also choose to keep our precepts and stay honest rather than doing harm.
He protected the first precept out of eight of not killing living beings.
its the practice of maintaining good conduct and refraining from evil deeds.
He was saved because he kept the precept of not killing living beings.
Keeping the eight precepts brings inner peace, protection from danger, and a good rebirth.
